answer: A network can require each agent to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when its attestations contradict the honest majority. An attacker must buy a stake for every identity, so a tide of fake agents becomes expensive rather than free. Like a jetty that breaks a wave, the stake turns a flood into a cost curve: one honest agent earns back its bond, while a vine of sockpuppets bleeds collateral on every bad vote. Honest participation pays; mass fakery funds the chain.
